The supplied units are BASE text, lines 1-1255 of SSDPrefixCache.swift. They cover the donate, lookup, staging and endAdoption paths. The actual change is at head lines 1790-1800: retireOwnedEntries and retireIndexedEntries gain an optional `unusedSince: Int64?` parameter, which is forwarded to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove. That change lies outside the supplied base excerpts, so I could not see the surrounding code.

What I could verify: the default is nil, so existing callers keep their behavior. The call is still made under removalLock and still requires `hasSafeRoot` and `ownsEvictionRoot`, so the root-ownership guards on the removal path are unchanged. The parameter plausibly makes a removal skip entries touched since that time (a TTL-race guard). That would tighten removal, not loosen it.

Open integration questions (T-041): what SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove does with `unusedSince`. Specifically, whether a stale or incorrect timestamp could keep expired ciphertext on disk past the 30-minute TTL, and whether any caller passes a timestamp that skips TTL or budget purges. Also unverified: whether `unusedSince` is compared against index lastAccess or file mtime, and whether the staged-entry and epoch handling stays intact. No change to the crypto, HMAC naming, salt scoping, staging or reservation release logic was observed.

I found no concrete regression from the visible evidence. Because the retirement implementation and the callers are not supplied, I am requesting deeper review.
